selection.description: Motivational essay counts in the quota 2 assessment, subject to the three-month rule.
190 study places in 2026, split 60 per cent quota 1 and 40 per cent quota 2. 2,093 applications in 2026, up 27 per cent on 2025.

requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

requirements.label: Language requirement: English A, or English B at 6.0 plus an English test

officialWording.text: You can only take a language test to fulfil the language requirement English level A if you have already passed English level B with a minimum grade of 6.0. … The IELTS Academic test must be passed with both an overall score of at least 7.0 and a minimum score of 6.0 for each of the four different sections. … The TOEFL iBT/ iBT Home Edition taken on or after 21 January 2026 must be passed with both a minimum overall score of at least 5 and a minimum score of 4,5 in each of the four different sections.

alternatives.label: An English test on top of English B at 5 or better in IB (Danish 6.0)
alternatives.note: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall and at least 6.0 in each section, or TOEFL iBT 5 overall and at least 4.5 in each (taken on or after 21 January 2026); Cambridge C1 Advanced 185 or C2 Proficiency 200 also count. CBS must have the result by 5 July, 12:00.

requirements.note: CBS application-and-admission page, read in a browser 25 Sep 2026. Cambridge C1 Advanced (185) or C2 Proficiency (200) meets both English B at 6.0 and the English A requirement. Test results must reach CBS by 5 July, 12:00; a test date may be at most two years old on 5 July.

alternatives.label: History of Ideas at B level
alternatives.subject: History of Ideas

officialRequirementsText.text: Specific entry requirements: English level B with a minimum grade of 6.0. Mathematics level B. History level B or International Economics level B or Social Studies level B or History of Ideas level B or Contemporary History level B. Language requirement: English level A. You must fulfil both the specific entry requirements and the language requirement to be eligible for the programme.

notes: Non-EU tuition at institution level: EUR 6,500 per semester (EUR 13,000 per year), or DKK 49,000 per semester (DKK 98,000 per year), for bachelor programmes. Application fee EUR 150 (approximately DKK 1,125) per applicant per admission round, payable by 15 March at 12.00 CET. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay neither.
